discovery: Optical detection and coherent control of single electron and nuclear spins in diamond (nitrogen-vacancy centers), founding solid-state quantum sensing
subfield: Quantum physics / solid-state spin qubits and quantum sensing
motivation: Wrachtrup and Jelezko first detected the magnetic resonance of a single nitrogen-vacancy defect optically. They went on to coherently control individual electron spins and their coupled nuclear spins in diamond at room temperature. This made a single atomic-scale defect in a solid into a qubit that can be read out, manipulated and kept coherent. Lukin, with Wrachtrup and others, then showed that this spin could serve as a nanoscale magnetometer, and he established nuclear-spin quantum registers and spin-photon interfaces. Together this work opened a new field: quantum sensing with solid-state spins. It now images magnetism in condensed-matter systems, probes single molecules and living cells, and supplies quantum-network nodes. It also started a wider search for defect qubits in silicon carbide and other hosts. Few discoveries have turned a fragile quantum property into such a widely used measurement tool.
